Extremely Disappointing Stay – Not What You Expect from Hilton

We visited Hilton Mumbai International Airport for a staycation to celebrate our toddler’s second birthday. Unfortunately, what was supposed to be a special and memorable occasion turned into a very disappointing experience. The overall service and hospitality were far below the standards expected from a reputed brand like Hilton.

Here are the major issues we faced during our stay:

1. Extremely Delayed Check-in: The check-in process was unnecessarily delayed. We were made to wait until 3:30 PM in the waiting area with our toddler. During this time, my wife requested a glass of water, but nobody bothered to provide it. This was a very basic expectation of hospitality, especially when guests are travelling with a small child.

2. Birthday Promise Not Fulfilled: Since we were visiting to celebrate our toddler’s second birthday, the hotel staff informed us that a complimentary pastry would be arranged as a birthday gesture. However, despite this assurance, we never received it during our stay. It was disappointing that even a small birthday gesture was overlooked.

3. Swimming Pool Under Renovation: The swimming pool was unavailable due to renovation. While we understand that maintenance work may be necessary, this significantly affected our staycation experience. Our toddler was looking forward to enjoying the pool, and with no such facility available, he became bored and restless inside the room. This was particularly disappointing for a birthday staycation.

4. Non-functional Bathtub and Arrogant Staff Behaviour: The bathtub in our room was not working due to a drainage issue. When I approached the reception, Mr. Rahul responded very arrogantly, saying that the system was busy and the issue could not be addressed immediately. Only after I raised a complaint through the Hilton Honors app was our room changed. To make matters worse, we had to carry some of our luggage ourselves because a luggage trolley was not available.

5. Extremely Poor Housekeeping Service: Housekeeping was another major disappointment. Calls were either unanswered or requests were fulfilled after unreasonable delays. For example, it took approximately 30 minutes to receive fresh towels and 20 minutes to get a dental kit. The staff showed very little urgency or concern for guest satisfaction, and their behaviour was far from welcoming.

A Few Positives:

There were only two things we genuinely appreciated:
- Since the hotel's swimming pool was unavailable, they offered us access to the swimming pool at ITC Maratha. This was a thoughtful alternative.
- The baby khichdi provided by the hotel was good and appreciated.

Overall Experience:

This was supposed to be a special birthday celebration for our little one, but unfortunately, the experience was filled with delays, inconvenience, poor service and disappointment.

From delayed check-in and unfulfilled birthday arrangements to non-functional room facilities and extremely slow housekeeping, almost every aspect of our stay fell short of expectations.

A hotel carrying the Hilton name should understand that hospitality is not just about the property or its brand reputation; it is about how guests are treated, especially families travelling with young children.

Honestly, this was one of our most disappointing hotel experiences. I would not recommend this property to families looking for a relaxing and memorable staycation, particularly when celebrating a special occasion.

I want to emphasise that the rest of the staff were lovely, and our overall experience with the hotel was very positive. **A Disappointing Stay at Sahara Star – Time for a Much-Needed Upgrade**

Every time we have stayed at Sahara Star, the experience has been pleasant and wonderful. Unfortunately, this visit was a major disappointment and felt like staying at a completely different hotel.

For a hotel that proudly calls itself an iconic property, the condition of the rooms is far below expectations. The rooms look dated and shabby, the furniture feels old, and the bed was extremely uncomfortable. The bathroom also looks outdated, and the shower quality was disappointing.

Even basic amenities lacked consistency. The electric kettle and tea-making setup did not meet expectations, drinking water was not replenished during our three-day stay, and there was no international charging adapter or suitable universal plug available. These are basic conveniences that guests should not have to worry about at a hotel of this stature.

The only real highlight of our stay was the view. However, a beautiful view alone cannot compensate for uncomfortable beds, outdated interiors, poor shower quality, and inadequate attention to essential amenities. Guests book a hotel for the overall experience, not just the view from the balcony.

Sahara Star urgently needs to invest in renovating its older rooms, upgrading its bathrooms and furniture, improving bedding quality, and ensuring consistent replenishment of basic amenities.

Having enjoyed wonderful stays here in the past, this experience was particularly disappointing. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and works towards restoring the standards and comfort that guests expect from an iconic hotel.

**A great view is not enough; the room, comfort, and service must live up to the hotel's reputation.**

I stayed at Trident Bandra Kurla for five nights while attending a conference at the nearby Jio World Convention Centre. At around AUD $400 per night, I found it difficult to justify the price, although the attentive service helped improve my overall impression.

Location and value for money

I chose Trident mainly because it was a five-minute walk from the convention centre. However, the walk was surprisingly unpleasant. There was no proper pedestrian crossing along my route, and crossing the busy road felt unsafe. Coming from Australia, I was surprised that a hotel at this price point had such poor pedestrian access to a major venue next door.

I also found that I gained little benefit from the hotel's facilities during my stay. My conference schedule was busy, and all my meetings and social activities with other attendees took place at the convention centre or nearby restaurants and cafés, rather than at the hotel. In practice, I was mostly using Trident as a place to sleep.

In hindsight, I would have preferred staying at a good four-star hotel within a 10-minute auto-rickshaw ride of the convention centre for half the price. The convenience of staying next door was not worth the premium.

Rooms and facilities

The room was comfortable and clean, but nothing exceptional for the price. I had stayed at Radisson Blu Mumbai International Airport for two nights beforehand, at roughly half the cost, and genuinely preferred its larger rooms, breakfast and overall experience.

Trident's breakfast buffet was good, with freshly prepared eggs, Indian dishes and coffee, but again, I felt Radisson Blu did it better.

The lobby also felt somewhat impersonal and lacked the welcoming, luxurious atmosphere I experienced at the Sofitel next door.

Service

The staff were generally friendly, polite and helpful. They consistently greeted guests warmly and responded well to requests. I also appreciated being allowed to use the third-floor shower facilities after checkout, as I had a late-night flight.

However, the laundry service was disappointing. On two separate occasions, I was told my laundry would be delivered by 7 pm, but it was late both times and I had to follow up myself. At around INR 500 (AUD $8) just to wash a T-shirt, I expected better reliability.

That said, I particularly appreciated how the hotel handled my feedback at checkout. The staff proactively asked whether there was anything they could have done to improve my stay. When I mentioned the laundry delays, they acknowledged the issue and offered a 15% discount on the laundry charges. It was a thoughtful gesture, and I appreciated that they took the feedback seriously and made an effort to address it.

One minor issue was that I was not able to work out how to adjust the shower temperature.

Overall

Trident Bandra Kurla is a comfortable hotel with friendly, attentive staff and good facilities. While I still don't think it offers particularly good value at AUD $400 per night, the quality of service deserves recognition. The staff's willingness to listen to feedback and offer a gesture of goodwill left me with a more positive impression of the hotel.

Excellent Location, Charming Ambience, but Food That Fell Short of Expectations

The location is undoubtedly ITC Maratha’s biggest advantage. In a city like Mumbai, being right next to the airport is a blessing, especially for travellers looking for a convenient stay or a transit hotel.

The hotel has beautiful architecture, and the rooms are comfortable, with a distinct retro-rustic charm that gives the property its own character. The overall ambience reflects the grandeur one would expect from ITC.

However, the food was a letdown.

My feedback is limited to the two breakfasts I had during my stay. I haven’t tried the lunch or dinner, so I cannot comment on those meals, which may well be better.

Having previously experienced the food at ITC Sonar Bangla, ITC Maurya Delhi, ITC Puri, ITC Bhubaneswar and the newer ITC property in Kolkata, I had fairly high expectations from ITC Maratha. Unfortunately, the breakfast experience did not quite live up to them.

The vada was cold and lacked the crispness one would expect, while the sabudana pearls were not properly cooked. The dosa was decent, and the chutneys and vermicelli were good. Overall, though, the food felt average compared with my experiences at other ITC properties.

Given ITC Maratha’s grandeur, reputation and time-tested hospitality standards, I expected a more satisfying culinary experience. Unfortunately, the breakfast did not leave the impression I had hoped for.

Would I return? Given its unbeatable proximity to the airport, I would certainly consider ITC Maratha for a short stay or as a transit hotel. However, based on my breakfast experience, the food alone would not be a reason for me to return.

A beautiful property in a fantastic location, but there is room for improvement when it comes to the breakfast experience.

I am sharing this feedback not merely over a disagreement about a breakfast discount, but because the overall experience fell short of the hospitality and guest care I associate with the Taj brand.

Lunch at Pondicherry Café, and it was quite an experience. An extensive spread with plenty of variety and some really good offerings. There's something to suit just about every palate, and you certainly won't be leaving hungry!

The dessert counter deserves a special mention. It's quite something and almost impossible to resist. In fact, saving room for dessert is highly recommended!

What also makes the experience enjoyable is the service. The staff are always alert, attentive and quick to respond - whether it's changing cutlery, checking on the table or answering any queries.
A special mention to Archana, who was particularly attentive. It's these little touches that make a difference to the overall dining experience.

A brilliant spread, warm hospitality and a dessert counter that's worth the visit in itself. Definitely a lovely place for a leisurely lunch in BKC.

Sofitel has consistently been the only hotel that manages to disappoint me with every visit. Following my previous stay, I had shared detailed feedback regarding the poor service and overall experience. After receiving an apology from the management, I decided to give the property another opportunity, genuinely hoping that corrective measures would have been implemented.

Unfortunately, nothing has changed. If anything, this visit has further reinforced my concerns about the hotel’s service standards, guest safety, and overall management accountability

1. Unprofessional and Rude Reception Staff

The hotel makes an excellent first impression with its ambience and interiors. However, that impression is immediately ruined by the attitude of the reception staff. Their behaviour was rude, unwelcoming, and completely inconsistent with the hospitality standards expected from a luxury hotel. A beautiful property means very little when basic courtesy and professionalism are missing.

2 Unacceptable Response to a Basic Request for My Baby

During my stay, I requested a blanket for my baby To my disbelief, I was bluntly informed that the hotel did not have one and that, since I was travelling with a baby, I should have brought my own

I find this response absolutely unacceptable. While I understand that certain amenities may be subject to availability, the dismissive manner in which the request was handled demonstrated a complete lack of empathy, courtesy, and hospitality. Is this genuinely how Sofitel expects its staff to treat families travelling with infants?

3. Failure to Release or Communicate the Pre-Authorisation at Checkout

This was not merely an inconvenience. It was a serious health and safety concern that could potentially have been avoided through appropriate communication and preventive measures

Guests should be informed in advance when chemical treatments are scheduled, particularly when such activities may affect individuals with respiratory conditions, allergies, infants, or other vulnerabilities

I expect the management to explain why guests were not notified and what safety precautions were implemented

I stayed at the Fairmont Mumbai in October 2026. While there was nothing seriously wrong with my stay, a number of small details fell short of what I would expect from a five-star hotel.

There is plenty to like. The hotel, completed in early 2025, is modern, with excellent facilities and well-appointed rooms. First impressions are good, but beyond the polished surroundings, two areas stood out as needing improvement.

Service: Staff were consistently courteous, but interactions often felt scripted and repetitive. I missed the personal touch that makes guests feel individually welcomed and looked after. Even a simple request for smaller notes proved surprisingly difficult: changing ₹1,000 involved three members of staff and took around ten minutes.

Dining: The restaurant was the biggest disappointment. The food was average, particularly given the prices, and the emphasis seemed to be on upselling rather than delivering a memorable meal. I was asked twice whether I wanted another drink while I was still only halfway through my current one. There is a fine line between attentive service and making guests feel pressured to order more.

Overall, the Fairmont Mumbai is an attractive hotel with considerable potential. However, more personalised service and a stronger dining experience would help it deliver the five-star standard its surroundings promise.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Wonderful first stay in India!

I spent my first two days in India at Radisson Blu Mumbai Airport, and it was a wonderful introduction to the country!

The staff were very friendly, welcoming, and attentive. One small gesture that stood out was when I was exploring the conference rooms upstairs. A staff member kindly gave me a short tour and pointed out some of the sights through the windows. It was a lovely personal touch.

Breakfast was a real highlight and absolutely worth it! Before coming to India, I was only familiar with dishes like butter chicken, dosa, and biryani back home in Australia. The breakfast buffet gave me a great chance to try many new Indian foods. There was an excellent variety, and the selection changed each day, so there was always something new to try.

You can also order freshly prepared Indian breakfast dishes and filter coffee made on the spot. I tried several dishes, and the masala dosa was easily my favourite!

The room was very comfortable, and the hotel grounds were beautiful. I especially liked the courtyard, with its well-maintained gardens and greenery. The rooftop pool area was equally lovely, with plenty of plants and a rather interesting view of the nearby railway line. It was surprisingly enjoyable watching the trains pass by!

My only minor complaint was that I found the chlorine in the swimming pool quite strong. It irritated my skin and eyes during my swim. Otherwise, the pool area was a great place to relax.

The location is also very convenient, around 10-15 minutes by car from the airport. Getting an Uber for pickup and drop-off was easy.

Overall, a fantastic stay with excellent service, great facilities, and especially memorable breakfasts. I would happily stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone visiting Mumbai!

Right from the security team at the entrance, the front desk, bellboys and housekeeping to the chefs and breakfast staff, everyone we interacted with was genuinely polite, helpful and always smiling. The food options were great too, particularly the breakfast. A special mention to the chefs and the breakfast team for their hospitality and the way they looked after us.

Honestly, what stood out the most for us was the staff. It’s one thing to have a beautiful property and good facilities, but it’s the people who really make a stay memorable, and this hotel gets that absolutely right.

A big thank you to the entire team at Radisson Blu Mumbai International Airport for making our stay so comfortable. We would happily stay here again and would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Mumbai!

Exceptional Hospitality – Akul and His Team Truly Went Above and Beyond!

Excellent service, exceptionally helpful staff, and a genuinely wonderful stay! What really stood out was the warmth, attentiveness, and thoughtfulness of Akul and his team, who went out of their way to ensure we were comfortable throughout our visit.

But what happened after we checked out is what truly sets this team apart.

We had inadvertently left a jacket behind at the hotel. Akul promptly called us, followed up on WhatsApp with photographs of the jacket, and asked whether we would like to have it couriered to us. He and his team then carefully kept the jacket safe until the courier arrived and ensured it was sent all the way to Pune, some 130 kilometres away!

Now, this wasn't just any jacket. It belonged to my wife's mother, was one of her favourites, and held considerable sentimental value. Its importance went well beyond the garment itself. What touched us most was that Akul and his team understood this immediately. They showed genuine empathy, took personal responsibility, and made sure it found its way back to us safely.

That, to me, is the true definition of exceptional hospitality. It's easy to provide good service while a guest is staying at your property. But to demonstrate the same care, concern, and commitment after the guest has checked out speaks volumes about the people and the service culture of the hotel.

A heartfelt thank you to Akul and his entire team. You didn't just return a forgotten jacket; you reunited our family with something that held precious memories.

Five stars without hesitation. Hospitality like this deserves recognition, and people like Akul and his team are the reason guests remember a hotel long after their stay. Highly recommended!

As a female solo traveller on a work trip, I felt extremely uncomfortable and unsafe at this property. The noise insulation is absolutely terrible, and instead of addressing this issue professionally, the hotel staff chose to accuse me of playing loud music and disturbing other guests when my TV was not even switched on.

What makes this experience even more frustrating is that the noise was coming from another room, yet the hotel staff failed to identify or appropriately address the actual source of the disturbance. Instead, I was unfairly targeted and subjected to an unnecessarily rude and confrontational phone call at 12:00 am, demanding that I turn down the volume for something I was not even responsible for. Rather than investigating the complaint or verifying the facts, the staff chose to harass me over an issue that was not originating from my room.

Even after I clearly explained my side of the story, there was no apology, no acknowledgment of their mistake, and absolutely no professionalism. The least one expects from a hotel is for its staff to investigate a complaint before accusing a guest and to communicate respectfully rather than making someone feel intimidated in their own room.

As a woman travelling alone for work, feeling safe and comfortable in my accommodation is particularly important. It is deeply disappointing that the staff’s approach made me feel the opposite. What is even more disheartening is that the staff member involved was herself a woman, yet showed no consideration or willingness to listen to another female guest travelling alone. Regardless of gender, every guest deserves fairness, courtesy, and respect.

Poor soundproofing is one issue, but failing to manage noise complaints appropriately, blaming the wrong guest, and refusing to acknowledge a mistake are entirely different matters. A hotel’s responsibility is to resolve disturbances fairly, not transfer the inconvenience onto an innocent guest.

There are far better properties that offer superior service, professional staff, and a more considerate environment. Based on this experience, I would not recommend this property, particularly to solo travellers who expect a peaceful, respectful, and hassle-free stay. The way a hotel handles a problem says far more about its standards than the problem itself, and unfortunately, this property fell well short of expectations.

A True Example of Exceptional Hospitality

I recently stayed for two nights at Fairfield by Marriott Mumbai International Airport. Although I serve as Regional Director of Finance overseeing Marriott hotels in South Texas, this was my first stay at a Fairfield property, and it made an excellent first impression. Although Fairfield is a four-star hotel, the service and overall experience exceeded many of the five-star experiences I have had around the world.

The transportation team was professional and courteous. The bellmen, doormen, and security team welcomed me warmly every time I entered or left the hotel. Their friendliness and consistent hospitality made me feel valued throughout my stay.

The food and beverage team was outstanding. The restaurant associates were attentive and made a point of greeting and thanking every guest. Rahul from room service was exceptionally friendly, professional, and helpful. He truly deserves special recognition.

My suite was spacious, beautifully prepared, and exceptionally clean. The entire property is very well maintained, and the attention to detail is evident throughout. Shashank, the Rooms Division Manager, was kind, attentive, and highly professional. General Manager Iftekhar Mehdi also took the time to meet with me and demonstrated genuine care for my experience.

The pool and surrounding area were clean, neat, and relaxing. The pool’s view overlooking the airport is a wonderful feature of the property. The fitness center was also spotless, well equipped, and very well maintained.

Many of the rooms overlook the airport, providing an excellent view of aircraft arriving and departing. You can watch the activity for hours without getting bored. Despite the hotel’s proximity to the airport, the soundproofing is excellent. I could not hear the aircraft from inside my room, allowing me to enjoy a quiet and comfortable stay.

As someone from a hotel-owning family—we operate two Le Royal Méridien properties in Chennai and Coimbatore—and as a hospitality professional who travels globally, I pay close attention to service, cleanliness, and hotel operations. During my stay, I observed several best practices that I plan to implement across my U.S. portfolio and share with our hotels in India.

What impressed me most was the genuine warmth of the team. Thank you to everyone who made my first Fairfield experience so memorable. I have already made another reservation for the end of this month and look forward to returning.

We had a wonderful stay at Meluha, the Fern in Powai staying for two nights—one before and one after our trip. What truly stood out was the warmth and helpfulness of the entire team, especially Siddhi, Jayshree, and Samarjeet. They went out of their way to make our stay comfortable, including upgrading our room as we were travelling as a family when better room was available. The rooms, especially the suites, are beautiful, spacious, and thoughtfully designed.

One of the most memorable moments was when we arrived at around 4 a.m. after our trip. Despite the early hour, the team welcomed us with smiling faces, immediately checked us in, and had even retained our details from our previous stay, making the process completely effortless. They arranged a lovely room for us to rest in without any delay. That level of genuine care and hospitality really made a difference.

The food was also very good. On our last morning, we were in a hurry and had only about 15 minutes before leaving, even though breakfast service had finished. The team still arranged a freshly prepared, piping-hot breakfast for us immediately. These small gestures of going above and beyond are what made our experience so special. A big thank you to Siddhi, Jaishree, Samarjeet, and the entire team—we truly felt cared for on both our stays and would happily return!

Disappointing Experience at Peninsula Grand Hotel

My overall stay at Peninsula Grand Hotel was good, and this was not my first visit. However, a few things during this stay left me disappointed, especially considering the hotel's reputation and standards.

Firstly, the central AC had cooling issues, which affected the room comfort. The bathtub was also not properly cleaned, which was quite unexpected from a hotel of this standard. Room service was fine, but overall room maintenance and housekeeping definitely need more attention.

The biggest disappointment was the minibar menu and billing confusion.

As per the minibar menu provided in the room, both Budweiser and Kingfisher Ultra were mentioned with a quantity of 2 and a rate of ₹325. Based on the way the information was presented, I understood that ₹325 was the price for two beers. However, the billing was based on individual units, resulting in a minibar charge of ₹715 on the final invoice.

My concern is not just about the amount but the lack of clarity in the menu. If ₹325 is the price per bottle, it should be clearly mentioned as a per unit price. Such basic pricing information should not be left open to interpretation, especially in a reputed hotel.

What disappointed me further was the way the management handled my concern. Instead of understanding the confusion and acknowledging that the menu could be clearer, the managers started explaining and justifying the existing menu. I was not expecting this kind of response from a hotel with such a reputation.

I even requested them to reprint the minibar menu with clearly mentioned quantities and per unit prices so that other guests do not face the same confusion in the future.

I am attaching photographs of the minibar menu and the invoice for reference.

I have visited this hotel before and genuinely expected a better experience. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the AC maintenance, bathroom cleanliness, room upkeep and, most importantly, transparency in minibar pricing.

A hotel with such a big name should focus not only on its facilities but also on clear communication, attention to detail and customer satisfaction. Unfortunately, this visit did not meet those expectations.

Ramada, Juhu – Disappointing for the Price
Ramada Juhu has a great location, and the rooms are spacious, but they badly need renovation. The breakfast is average, and the service leaves much to be desired. When you ask for a few basic items, being told that “this is not a buffet” is unacceptable for a hotel positioning itself as a luxury five-star property.
The crockery also needs serious improvement. The cups, in particular, looked more suited to a government guest house than a five-star hotel.
Overall, while the location is excellent, the dated rooms, average breakfast and disappointing service do not justify the price. The hotel is simply not worth what it charges.

Excellent Food, Wonderful Hospitality and a Memorable Dining Experience at Kohinoor Continental, Andheri

We had a wonderful dining experience at Kohinoor Continental, Andheri, Mumbai. The food was amazing, the service was warm, and the overall experience made our visit truly enjoyable.

A special appreciation to the chef for being so accommodating with our requests for a chicken tikka pizza and chicken tikka pasta. It is always refreshing when a restaurant is willing to go the extra mile to cater to its guests' preferences. The pasta was good, and the pizzas were equally enjoyable. If you are visiting, I would definitely recommend trying both!

The breakfast and brunch are also highly recommended. The morning breakfast was good, and it is the kind of experience you should take your time to enjoy rather than rush through. Whether you are planning a relaxed breakfast or a leisurely brunch, Kohinoor Continental is worth considering.

A special mention goes to Ayush, our server, who was an absolute delight. He was pleasant, attentive, and made us feel welcome throughout our meal. His service added a personal touch to the experience and genuinely made our visit memorable. Good hospitality is often what separates an ordinary meal from a great dining experience, and Ayush certainly made a difference.

Overall, we were thoroughly impressed by the food, the chef's willingness to accommodate our requests, and the quality of the service.

My recommendations: Try the chicken tikka pizza, chicken tikka pasta, and definitely make time for the breakfast or brunch. Also, a big shout-out to Ayush for making our dining experience even better!

Highly recommended for anyone looking for good food and warm hospitality in Andheri. We enjoyed our visit and would happily return!

Extremely Disappointing Experience – Not Worth a 4-Star Rating

This hotel does not deserve a 4-star rating. I am giving it 1 star only because that is the lowest possible rating and because at least one sensible and supportive person at the reception was willing to listen and help.

I had booked a room for 3 nights and arrived for check-in at around 2 AM. The receptionist gave me a key, but it didn't work. When I requested another key, he sent me upstairs with a housekeeping staff member who was supposed to open the door using a master key. Even the master key didn't work because the door lock was faulty.

I went downstairs 4 times, explaining that the problem was clearly with the lock, not the key. However, the night receptionist refused to understand and repeatedly sent me upstairs with different keys. After 3–4 attempts and unnecessary arguments, the housekeeping staff finally opened the door using a physical key. When I explained that I couldn't go through this process every time I wanted to enter my room during my 3-night stay, the receptionist simply insisted that there was no issue with the lock or key. Absolutely shocking customer service.

I requested a room change, but was told no room was ready. Eventually, they gave me a lower-category room meant for single occupancy, with a transparent bathroom, despite my travelling with a colleague. They promised to change it in the morning. The entire check-in and room-lock drama took around 30–40 minutes in the middle of the night.

In the morning, a different and helpful receptionist agreed to provide us with a twin-bed room with a proper bathroom. However, when my colleague arrived around 3 PM, the room was still not ready. Despite having booked 3 nights, with one night already gone, we had to wait until around 6 PM to finally get the room.

Unfortunately, the poor service continued even after checkout. We accidentally left some clothes and belongings in the room, but nobody informed us. When I called around 7 PM, the staff initially claimed they had no information about any items and said they would check with the daytime housekeeping staff the following morning.

I asked them to check the lost and found or contact the relevant staff, as I had to leave. They promised to get back to me, but nobody contacted me for 4 hours. When I called again, the night receptionist was extremely rude, spoke loudly, refused to check, claimed nothing was there, and abruptly disconnected the call.

Even the following morning, nobody provided an update until around 11 AM, when I called again. Only then did they finally confirm that my belongings were there.

The hotel clearly lacks basic coordination between reception and housekeeping. Found belongings should be reported, and guests should receive proper updates. Instead, I had to repeatedly follow up for something that should have been handled professionally.

The breakfast options were also very limited.

Overall, the service was pathetic. Particularly, the night reception staff were unhelpful, unwilling to understand logical concerns, and more interested in arguing with guests than solving problems.

I booked this hotel after seeing its positive reviews and had high expectations, but the actual experience was extremely disappointing. I am surprised how this property maintains such positive ratings.

If you only want a budget-friendly stay with a decent room and don't care much about service, you may consider it. Otherwise, I would strongly recommend avoiding this hotel.

A hotel is not just about providing a room; hospitality is about how you treat guests and resolve their problems. Unfortunately, this hotel failed miserably at that.

Disappointing Stay – Not Worth the Premium Price

We booked a two-day stay at Dragonfly Hotel - The Art Hotel, after seeing the pictures online, which made the hotel look impressive. While the exterior looks amazing, the actual room experience was quite disappointing and did not live up to our expectations.

We were promised a premium room, but the only noticeable extras were a smart TV and a JBL speaker. Apart from that, the room had a bed, a table, and a basic stand for clothes. There was no proper cupboard or wardrobe, and the only mirror was a small one in the bathroom. This made getting ready inconvenient, as you had to keep going back and forth to the bathroom. For a room sold at a premium price, we expected much better facilities and comfort.

We had booked for two days, but after experiencing the room, we wanted to cancel the second day. We were informed that the cancellation policy required 72 hours' notice, even though we had made the booking just a day earlier. Unfortunately, we were unable to cancel and had to complete the stay.

Another disappointing aspect was the reception staff, whose behaviour we found rude and unwelcoming. However, I genuinely want to appreciate the housekeeping staff, who were extremely good, helpful, and courteous. They were the highlight of our stay.

We chose this hotel based on the positive reviews we had read, but our experience did not match those expectations. I cannot comment on whether the reviews are genuine, but I would strongly advise future guests to check the actual room facilities carefully and clarify the cancellation policy before booking.

Overall, the hotel looks much better from the outside than the experience it offers inside. We paid a premium price but did not receive a premium experience. Please don't book based on the pictures alone.
